text:
support_jessie: Heads up — Customer ACME reported a 2m window of 504s and client timeouts during a traffic spike at 14:03 UTC. They saw ~15% failed requests. They escalated to sales. Request IDs: req_12a3, req_12a4, req_12b0.

oncall_miguel: Thanks. Can you paste one of the failing request logs and the approximate QPS?

support_jessie: QPS peaked ~120/s for that tenant. Log sample (from gateway):
```
[14:03:12] req=req_12a3 upstream_status=504 latency_ms=4500 path=/v1/generate model=redwood-medium tenant=acme
[14:03:13] req=req_12a4 upstream_status=504 latency_ms=5000 error="upstream timeout after 5s"
```

sre_kate: I'm seeing a scale-up lag on the serving pool that handles that tenant. KEDA metric shows queue length spiking but scaledobject stayed at 0->1 for ~40s, podReady delayed until ~90s because model init took long. HPA didn't kick because scaledobject minReplica=0 and cooldown is 60s.

eng_infra_ryan: Pasted kube output:
```
ScaledObject/acme-worker scaledReplicas=0 desired=3 lastScaleTime=14:02:25
HPA/acme-worker currentReplicas=0 desiredReplicas=0 CPU% 10
Pods:
 - acme-worker-0 Initializing
 - acme-worker-1 CrashLoopBackOff (model fetch timeout)
```

sre_kate: Also saw readiness probe failing on init: readiness endpoint returns 503 until model warmup done. Model warmup ~60-80s for that config.

auth_liz: Not seeing auth failures; tokens validated. Billing service did have a brief outage ~14:01 but recovered; I don't think it's directly killing requests but could have delayed some token checks — low impact.

eng_infra_ryan: Repro hypothesis: combination of (a) ScaledObject min=0 + KEDA poll interval/cooldown > request window, (b) long model init + readiness guard, (c) HPA metrics not seeing the queue because metric adapter uses pod count. Leads to coldstart and 5xx spikes.

support_jessie: Customer reports most errors were on long requests (>=4s). They retry and get timeouts. They're asking for short-term mitigation.

dana_pm: Short-term mitigations: 1) bump ScaledObject minReplica to 2 for that tenant, 2) reduce KEDA cooldown/pollInterval to 10s, 3) add an immediate fallback routing to smaller quantized model for that tenant while warmup completes. Which can we do quickly?

oncall_miguel: I can patch ScaledObject and set minReplica=2 for acme now. Will monitor. Also propose lowering readiness threshold to accept traffic earlier with degraded quality? Risky.

sre_kate: Patch applied: ScaledObject minReplica=2. New pods started, model init still ~70s but we have capacity coming up so client success rate improved after 60s.

incident-bot: Incident created INC-4279: "ACME 504s during burst — autoscale warmup lag" assigned to eng-infra + SRE.

eng_infra_ryan: Follow-up infra action items: - Add warmup endpoint to serve a light-weight health that can be ready earlier; - Add model initialization tracing + histogram to console; - Consider a fast-start model variant to serve fallbacks; - Revisit default ScaledObject minReplica for tenants above X QPS.

auth_liz: I'll confirm that billing token outage had no cascading effect.

support_jessie: Customer updated: errors dropped from 15% -> 1.2% after minReplica patch, still want guarantee. They're asking for config guidance to avoid this in future.

dana_pm: We'll document recommended defaults: minReplica=1 or 2 for predictable tenants, KEDA cooldown <=15s for bursty patterns, and include a recommended warmup probe. Assigning doc ticket DOC-803.

oncall_miguel: Marking incident as mitigated for now, will keep ticket open until postmortem and follow-ups done.

sre_kate: Note: we should also add a gating rule in console alerts when queue length > X and currentReplicas=0 to auto-escalate.

support_jessie: Thanks all — I'll ping customer with the mitigation summary and INC-4279 ref. :thumbsup:
